items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: I mean, you'd see, even Tishockey, he would talk about musicians, but you'd turn around and he'd help somebody, you know?

ctx.x: No, I think there are less musicians coming up.

I don't think it's nearly the same now with the ones, the old timers dying off, you know. But the old timers, I mean, there was just something about those musicians. I mean, I don't know. Even though they may have been terrible, they may have hated you. But when you were around them, if they thought you needed them, they'd be the first ones to help you, you know? It was that kind of a thing. And this is what was so great about them. I mean, you'd see, even Tishockey, he would talk about musicians, but you'd turn…

Bill Crayton and we used to figure out, and we can talk about this after the tapes over, an all-star band where you'd get together. Everybody created jazz and the whole mix of that, each one, you know? They would have made a good band, except they'd have hated each other.
